subject: Initial benchmarking plan and acceptance criteria for Velocity Apps onboarding
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@velocityapps.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@velocityapps.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmarks we need to validate for go-live

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency numbers you showed. Before we lock a go-live date, infra wants a brief, reproducible acceptance checklist and a load-run we can sign off on. High level asks from our SRE:
- Target production pattern: 200 sustained RPS with 1.5k token average payloads during peak windows.
- p95 latency under 220ms for single-turn text generation.
- Error rate under 0.2% (5xx + client timeouts).
- Graceful degradation to the fallback model if utilization hits the reserved cap.

Can you share a plan and a suggested test window next week? We can provision a staging API key and a sample traffic file (will attach).

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, Velocity Apps

Attachment: velocity_traffic_sample_v0.csv (CSV, 18 KB)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@velocityapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarks we need to validate for go-live

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear requirements and the sample traffic. I’ve sketched a lightweight, reproducible benchmark playbook below and attached a formal plan PDF. Summary of the approach:

1) Acceptance criteria (proposed, can be tightened):
- Sustained throughput: 200 RPS sustained over 15 minutes (traffic-shaped to your peak profile).
- Latency: p50 < 60ms, p90 < 140ms, p95 < 220ms (single-turn generation, 1.5k tokens).
- Error budget: total error rate (5xx + client timeouts) < 0.2% during the run.
- Fallback behavior: requests beyond reserved capacity must route to the configured fallback model with clear headers and <= 500ms added latency.

2) Test plan (high level):
- Environment: Redwood staging cluster (isolated stack, same instance types as dedicated pool).
- Credentials: we will issue a staging API key scoped to Velocity Apps.
- Dataset: use your attached traffic sample; we'll synthesize tokens to match length distribution.
- Load generator: k6 + custom prefix-caching probes; we’ll also run a KV-cache warmup pass.
- Observability: token-level latency, model-level QPS, 5xx counts, and Redis/KV hit rates streamed to a shared dashboard.

3) Roles & schedule:
- Redwood: Maya (lead), Ben (benchmark execution & observability), Neha (results analysis + quality checks).
- Velocity: Alex (SRE owner), Priya (app traffic SME).
- Proposed windows: Tue 28 Jul 09:00–11:00 PT (smoke + 2 load passes) or Thu 30 Jul 13:00–15:00 PT (full run).

4) Deliverables:
- Raw run artifacts (k6 logs, request traces).
- Dashboard link with token-level breakdown.
- A concise acceptance report with pass/fail, deviation notes, and remediation suggestions.

I attached: velocity_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf (detailed step-by-step) and traffic-shape-sample.csv (normalized input). Please confirm which window you prefer and whether we should run the p95-sensitive pass first or the throughput ramp first.

Best,

Maya Srinivasan
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachments: velocity_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 42 KB); traffic-shape-sample.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@velocityapps.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarks we need to validate for go-live

Adding a couple of practical notes from an execution perspective:
- Warmup: we recommend a 10-minute KV-cache warmup at ~50% of target RPS before each measured run. That avoids cold-cache variability.
- Ramp profile: 0 → 50 → 100 → 150 → 200 RPS in 5-minute steps, hold at 200 RPS for 15 minutes.
- Health checks: we’ll keep a separate light probe hitting the health endpoint every 15s and record 4xx/5xx.
- Fallback verification: during the third minute at peak we’ll introduce a small artificial throttling to a subset of requests to verify model routing/fallback path.

Also calling out a couple of acceptance-edge items we see in previous customer runs:
- Tokenization variance: send a 100-example sample to validate the 1.5k token assumption.
- Burst windows: if you have short spikes (30s) >200RPS we’ll need to size burst capacity or confirm SLA behavior.

I’ll own the runbook steps and the dashboard wiring. Maya — once Alex confirms a window Ben and I will sync on the exact run order and share the dashboard link in advance.

Thanks,
Ben
Benchmarking Engineer | Redwood Inference

We’re good to proceed on those conditions. Please send the staging API key and dashboard link when ready.

- Alex: confirm we should use the dedicated pool config you approved in the procurement doc (VD-5492).
- Velocity: whitelist the staging API key below:
